title: Largest square of free roof
prompt:
A roof is mapped as a grid. A cell holding 1 is free and a cell holding 0 has a vent or a skylight. Solar panels come only in square blocks, so return the area of the largest square made entirely of free cells. Return 0 if no cell is free.

- grid has 1 to 200 rows and 1 to 200 columns; every row has the same length.
- Each cell is 0 or 1.
hints: Let side(r, c) be the side of the largest free square whose bottom-right corner is at (r, c).
A square of side k ending at (r, c) needs squares of side k − 1 ending above, to the left and diagonally up-left. So side(r, c) = 1 + min of those three, for a free cell.
Track the largest side as you go and return its square. Two rows of the table are enough.

solution.explanation: This is grid DP on square corners. For a free cell, the largest square ending there is limited by its three neighbours up, left and up-left: if any of them supports only a smaller square, the gap shows up in that direction. So the side is 1 plus their minimum, and 0 for a blocked cell. Filling row by row keeps the three inputs ready. The answer is the largest side seen, squared. A padded column 0 removes the edge checks.

complexity.notes: Each cell takes constant work. Only the previous row and the current row are kept.

followUps: Count all free squares of every size instead of the largest one.
Find the largest free rectangle instead of a square.
